rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategic themes recur in Key Concepts — ≥2-3 module-specific theme instances
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule prevents: a module teaching tactics with no visible worldview underneath. Walked all 4 Key Concepts bullets (lines 48-51, unchanged) against the strategy doc's 6 recurring themes (§Recurring themes): bullet 1 ('the audit ranked the thin spots... filled the worst two or three') and bullet 4 ('the run started from a pinned commit... an experiment, not a production run') both instance theme 2, compounding — strategy's Mood-arc section states verbatim 'Every send-off is an experiment, not a production run you need to get right first time'; bullet 3 ('Traces are data. Stopping... is reading, not failing') instances theme 4, mechanically-self-aware/grain-of-salt — 'ask, then verify against the artifact... the actual behavior,' and the trace IS the artifact here. Two distinct themes across 3 of 4 bullets clears the ≥2-3 floor (floor reads 'ge 2-3'; two themes is sufficient, and the rule does not require every bullet to carry one). Note (non-blocking): strategy's own 'Themes earned' line for M4 also names mirror ('the un-packaged run will reflect your actual prompting + memory quality straight back'), which does not surface explicitly in Key Concepts — not required since the floor is already met and mirror is not mandatory-per-bullet.
